nodes.name: Conventional Calcination
nodes.procedure: Harzandi et al. reported the synthesis of a Ru core-shell structure regulated by Ni single-atom dopants (Ni-Ru@RuOx) via calcination at 400°C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: Harzandi et al. reported the synthesis of a Ru core-shell structure regulated by Ni single-atom dopants (Ni-Ru@RuOx) via calcination at 400°C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Molten Salt Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Wang et al. successfully synthesized tantalum (Ta) single-atom-doped RuO2 (Ta-RuO2, Ta: 2.5 wt.%) using molten NaNO3 as the solvent at a processing temperature of 350°C.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al. successfully synthesized tantalum (Ta) single-atom-doped RuO2 (Ta-RuO2, Ta: 2.5 wt.%) using molten NaNO3 as the solvent at a processing temperature of 350°C.

nodes.name: Dual Molten Salt Doping
nodes.procedure: Tang et al. successfully achieved dual doping of RuO2 using a mixture of molten NaNO3 and KNO3. The team revealed that both the incorporated palladium (Pd) and cobalt (Co) are highly monodisperse within the RuO2 lattice (PdCo-RuO2, Pd: 0.9 wt.% Co: 0.38 wt.%).
nodes.source_text: Tang et al. successfully achieved dual doping of RuO2 using a mixture of molten NaNO3 and KNO3.

nodes.name: High Temperature Molten Salt
nodes.procedure: Tang et al. synthesized unique 3R-phase IrO2 materials (group space: R3m No.166) that differ from the conventional rutile-phase structure, in which a low loading of ruthenium (Ru) was doped into the lattice by substitutional doping (H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4, Ru: 1.12±0.13 at.%). The product was obtained at 950°C using Li2CO3 as the solvent.
nodes.source_text: The product was obtained at 950°C using Li2CO3 as the solvent.

nodes.name: Molten Salt Nb-doped IrO2
nodes.procedure: Ke et al. prepared a type of 1T-phase IrO2 by introducing a low loading of niobium (Nb) (Nb0.05Ir0.95O2, Nb: 5 wt.%) using molten K2CO3 as the solvent at 800°C.
nodes.source_text: using molten K2CO3 as the solvent at 800°C.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis

nodes.name: Sol-Gel Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Liu et al. synthesized niobium (Nb)-doped RuO2 nanoparticles (Nb0.1Ru0.9O2, Nb: 13.44 at.%) using polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP) and ethanol as the coordination agent/solvent.

nodes.name: Co-precipitation Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Wang et al. obtained multi-crystalline spherical IrOx nanoparticles with the incorporation of a low content of titanium (Ti-IrOx/Ir, Ti:1.92 wt.%). The team applied CTAB as a cationic surfactant and TiB2 as a Ti source.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images reveal Ru core-shell structure regulated by Ni single-atom dopants in Ni-Ru@RuOx catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Harzandi et al. reported the synthesis of a Ru core-shell structure regulated by Ni single-atom dopants (Ni-Ru@RuOx) via calcination at 400°C for 2h.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images of Ta-RuO2 reveal coexistence of amorphous and crystalline domains with short-range ordered and isolated Ta atoms indicating high dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images (Figure 3b,c) revealed the existence of short-range ordered Ta atoms and isolated Ta atoms, indicating the high dispersion of incorporated Ta by substitutional doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image of Ta-RuO2 and PdCo-RuO2 confirm high dispersion of incorporated Ta, Pd and Co by substitutional doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: c) Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM image of Ta-RuO2. d) HAADF-STEM image of PdCo RuO2. e) Magnified HAADF-STEM image with elemental line scanning...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM combined with Ru K-edge EXAFS verifies dispersion of atomic Ru in the Ir-O lattice of H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM combined with Ru K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis verified the dispersion of atomic Ru in the Ir-O lattice (Figure 3h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images with intensity analysis confirm atomic dispersion in H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: g) HAADF-STEM images with corresponding intensity analysis for H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra at Ru K-edge confirm atomic Ru dispersion in H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: h) FT-EXAFS spectra at the Ru K-edge for H3.8Ir1-xRuxO4 and the comparison samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms atomic Pt substitution within RuO2 lattice of Pt-RuO2, inducing compressive strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM confirmed atomic Pt substitution within the RuO2 lattice, which induced compressive strain in the Ru-Ru distances near the Pt sites (Figure 4a,b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image confirms atomic dispersion of V atoms and V dimers in Vn-RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: c) HAADF-STEM image confirming the atomic dispersion of V atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra confirm atomic dispersion of Nb in RuO2 lattice of Nb0.1Ru0.9O2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nb K-edge FT-EXAFS spectra revealed the atomic dispersion of Nb in the RuO2 lattice (Figure 4f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals coexistence of metal Ru and RuO2 lattice structures in RuSbOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM clearly revealed the coexistence of metal Ru and RuO2 lattice structures (Figure 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Enlarged HAADF-STEM images with Sb single atoms marked confirm monodispersion of Sb in RuSbOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: h) Enlarged HAADF-STEM images with Sb single atoms marked by red and yellow cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and line profile scattering signals confirm atomic Ti substitutional doping in Ti-IrOx/Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and the scattering signals in the line profile confirmed the occurrence of atomic Ti through substitutional doping (Figure 5b).
